AAPL.rationale: Apple's Q2 FY2026 results show solid fundamental health: revenue of $111.18B (+16.6% YoY), EPS of $2.01 (+21.8% YoY), and record Services revenue of ~$31B (+16% YoY) with 76.7% gross margins. The company generated $28.7B in operating cash flow for the quarter, maintains a strong balance sheet with $106.5B in equity and a net cash position of ~$62B, and recently authorized a $100B buyback with a dividend increase. However, several factors temper enthusiasm. The stock trades at a P/E of 37.5x, near the upper end of its 30-43x 12-month range, and P/B of 43.2x is elevated. The QoQ trajectory is negative (revenue -22.7%, EPS -29.2%) reflecting normal seasonality after the holiday quarter, but the TTM picture is incomplete due to fiscal calendar gaps. Regulatory headwinds are material: the Supreme Court rejected Apple's App Store appeal in April 2026, the EU DMA fine of €500M stands, and India's antitrust probe continues — all threatening the high-margin Services business. The leadership transition from Tim Cook to John Ternus introduces execution risk. Rising 10-year Treasury yields (4.45%) and elevated oil prices ($92.65/bbl) create macro headwinds for a stock trading at a premium multiple. The Q3 guidance of 14-17% YoY growth is encouraging, and the stock has rallied +14.5% over the past quarter, but much of the good news appears priced in at current valuations. The near-term catalyst of the Q2 earnings beat (April 30) has already been absorbed. Net: solid franchise with durable competitive advantages, but valuation is fair-to-slightly-rich vs its own history, and regulatory/leadership risks prevent a higher score.
